nodes.name: FeNiCuWRu HEA nanoparticle synthesis
nodes.procedure: FeNiCuWRu nanoparticles (NPs) were synthesized by reduction of metal salts mediated by organic solvent at low temperature of 130 °C with complexing agent. The method enables uniform nucleation and growth of metal elements and promotes formation of single-phase solid solution. Similar structures were observed for FeNiCuWRu grown on titanium foam and nickel foam.

unit_operations.name: Metal salt reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: an organic solvent is used to mediate the reduction of metal salts

unit_operations.name: Nucleation and growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The low temperature of 130 °C enables uniform nucleation and growth of the metal elements

nodes.source_text: In this work, an organic solvent is used to mediate the reduction of metal salts and provide a controlled environment for atomic diffusion. The low temperature of 130 °C enables uniform nucleation and growth of the metal elements, while the use of a complexing agent significantly reduces the Gibbs free energy, thereby promoting the formation of a single-phase solid solution (Fig. S1, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiCuWRu nanoparticles show three main peaks at 44.1°, 51.5°, and 76.1° corresponding to (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of face-centered cubic (fcc) structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The three main peaks of FeNiCuWRu nanoparticles (NPs) are located at 44.1°, 51.5°, and 76.1° (Fig. 2a), corresponding to the (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of a characteristic face-centered cubic (fcc) structure, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomically resolved HAADF-STEM image shows lattice fringes with 0.2 nm spacing indexed to (111) crystal plane, abundant grain boundaries, and stacking faults with local tensile strains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A representative atomic-resolution image of a HEA NP along the [1-10] zone axis is displayed in Fig. 2c... HAADF-STEM reveals distinct lattice fringes of FeNiCuWRu-NP, with a lattice spacing of 0.2 nm, indexed to the (111) crystal plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental maps show Fe, Ni, Cu, W, and Ru are evenly distributed without obvious element segregation, confirming single-phase solid solution alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy mapping (Fig. 2g and Fig. S4c, ESI†) shows that the five components in the quinary nano-alloy are evenly distributed without obvious element segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows FeNiCuWRu composition as Fe:Ni:Cu:W:Ru ≈ 8:38:20:11:23 mass ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The composition of FeNiCuWRu-NPs was analyzed using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). The mass ratio was found to be approximately Fe : Ni : Cu : W : Ru ≈ 8 : 38 : 20 : 11 : 23.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows metallic and oxidized states: Fe (Fe0 at 706.70 eV, Fe2+ at 710.58 eV, Fe3+ at 712.38 eV), Ni (Ni0 at 852.98/874.08 eV, Ni2+ at 856.18/878.28 eV), Cu (Cu0 at 932.88/952.78 eV, Cu2+ at 934.68/954.98 eV), W6+ at 36.05/38.15 eV, Ru (Ru0 at 462.77/484.40 eV, Ru4+ at 464.80/486.90 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis verifies the presence of iron, nickel, copper, tungsten, ruthenium and oxygen... XPS spectra of (i) Fe 2p, (j) Ni 2p, (k) Cu 2p, (l) W 4f, and (m) Ru 3p of FeNiCuWRu, FeNiWRu, and FeNiRu-NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows FeNiCuWRu has smallest charge transfer resistance Rct of 1.47 Ω (HER) and 1.65 Ω (OER), FeNiWRu has 11.12 Ω (HER) and 2.60 Ω (OER), FeNiRu has 20.21 Ω (HER) and 4.33 Ω (OER).
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeNiCuWRu exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct) value of 1.47 Ω, compared to FeNiWRu (11.12 Ω) and FeNiRu (20.21 Ω)... FeNiCuWRu exhibits the smallest Rct value of 1.65 Ω among this group of catalysts (FeNiWRu: 2.60 Ω, FeNiRu: 4.33 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows HEA-FeNiCuWRu nanoparticles are uniformly cross-linked.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis, the HEA-FeNiCuWRu nanoparticles were observed to be uniformly cross-linked (Fig. S2a, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern proves the fcc crystal structure of HEA-NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern further proves the fcc crystal structure of HEA-NPs (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) shows significant local tensile strains near stacking faults in FeNiCuWRu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Indeed, significant local tensile strains were observed near the stacking faults in FeNiCuWRu through geometric phase analysis (GPA) (Fig. 2f and Fig. S5, ESI†).
